segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: In the moment I went with unit count — Order A first — partly because that's our default rule when picking between two rush jobs.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The planner considered the tighter packaging slot and selected Order A using an explicit production rule; the generation specification treats this as plausible domain reasoning, not an intentional bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I decided to just treat Line 3 as available overflow capacity if Line 1 or Line 2 fell behind, and moved on to the next issue.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is the planned Bounded Rationality instance: under concurrent demands, the planner accepted the first workable assessment and did not check the readily available Order C dependency before committing Line 3.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I decided to provisionally build the buffer units into the Order B plan rather than wait, because waiting with no ETA on a callback risked losing time I couldn't get back.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The planner made a reversible provisional plan under uncertain QA timing and explicitly planned to adjust if QA flagged an issue; this is treated as reasonable operational planning.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Overtime plus talking to the carrier directly gave me a shot at getting the full order out with minimal disruption, even shipping a few minutes past official cutoff.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The planner explicitly weighed overtime, partial shipment, and renegotiation, then made a documented cost and customer-service trade-off; the generation specification does not mark this as biased.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision to commit Line 3 as overflow capacity after accepting the operator's informal alarm assessment without checking Order C's dependency.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Acceptance of the first satisfactory option under multi-threaded time pressure, foregoing a readily available check of Order C's dependency on Line 3 output because exhaustive verification exceeded practical time and attentional capacity.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Attentional tunneling is a related attention-narrowing construct, but it is not an approved alias for Bounded Rationality. The benchmark requires the exact target label or an established equivalent for a strict true positive.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures the defining omission: under concurrent demands and time pressure, attention remained on the two salient rush orders and the planner did not perform the readily available Line 3 schedule check for Order C. It also identifies the affected schedule-monitoring/evidence-search operation. This is a full mechanism match even though the taxonomy label differs.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted participant statements are present, correctly attributed, and substantively support the reported narrowed focus, omitted schedule check, and retrospective acknowledgment.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The quote is valid and localized to the correct episode, but the candidate proposes recall-based availability or normalcy reasoning about prior alarm episodes. It does not establish the hidden first-workable-option and omitted-dependency-check mechanism. It is also considered only after identified findings, and obs_001 already claims the hidden instance.

The candidate is localized to a negative decision episode and describes a possible reluctance to choose partial shipment or renegotiation. The interview instead documents an explicit operational trade-off among alternatives, with no hidden instance at this location.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: The RAG detected the sole positive reasoning segment with no false alarms through all identified-confidence thresholds; candidate inclusion adds one false alarm.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: No strict true positive: the identified finding is correctly localized with a full mechanism match but uses the unapproved near-neighbor label Attentional tunneling instead of Bounded Rationality.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: One mechanism-first true positive at every threshold: the reported mechanism and evidence fully match the hidden Bounded Rationality instance.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidates add no true positives. Availability heuristic is a useful but incomplete near-miss; Plan continuation bias is unsupported speculation on a negative segment and lowers fourth-threshold precision.

Two candidate findings add false-positive burden when candidates are counted.

overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows a taxonomy gap rather than a failure to detect the manifested reasoning pattern: strict identification is zero because of the label mismatch, while mechanism-first identification is perfect before candidate inclusion.
